summary: Streaming reconnect sequence-number wrap suppresses terminal fragment
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when a streaming session reconnects after a short network flap, the final (terminal) fragment of the response is missing. The session appears to have completed server-side, but the client never receives the terminal 'end' chunk. Impact: Several of Neptune Analytics' production inference pipelines are returning incomplete reports to end users; customers are seeing truncated paragraphs or missing final sentences. Observation: Logs indicate reconnect attempts where the session sequence number wraps (increments overflow) and the session-manager accepts the reconnect but logs an overlapping seqnum window; downstream delivery to the websocket/SSE channel omits the 'terminal' event. This is reproducible under a high-frequency reconnect pattern and has been seen with both SSE and websocket clients.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a long-running streaming call to /v1/streams using gpt-redwood-3b with streaming=true.
2) Simulate periodic network drops (150-500ms) from the client every ~12-20s until the model emits final tokens.
3) Allow the client to automatically reconnect using the session token and resume mechanism.
4) Observe that sometimes the server-side logs show the stream completed, but the client never receives the terminal 'end' chunk and the payload is truncated.
Notes: issue appears more likely when reconnects happen frequently and when the session sequence counter on session-manager crosses a 32-bit boundary (wrap).

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: 32-bit unsigned sequence counter overflow causes server-side session-manager to wrap to 0. Outbound multiplexer computes a relative window to decide whether to emit events; the wrapped terminal event falls outside the computed window and is dropped.
Reproduced: Yes, in local cluster by artificially incrementing client_seq to 2^32-2 and triggering a reconnect during the final token emission.

Scope: Affects both SSE and websocket transports because session-manager sequence handling is transport-agnostic. Likely triggered only for very long-lived sessions or extremely frequent reconnect patterns. Observed for gpt-redwood-3b and open-llama-7b (models that produce long outputs).
Risk: Low to medium frequency but high customer impact when it occurs (final conclusion missing). Could affect other customers with high reconnect rates in older clients that reuse 32-bit counters.
Next steps: (a) implement 64-bit counters and roll out; (b) add unit test that simulates wrap; (c) add metric for seqwrap events and outbound-drops-by-reason.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (customer-private): increase session.replay_window to 96 and enable 'seqwrap_tolerant' flag in session-manager. Neptune reports initial mitigation effective.
Planned fix: roll internal libs to use 64-bit monotonic sequence counters for session-manager and outbound multiplexer. Will include compatibility shim for older persisted session tokens.

Rollout plan: Patch in canary (low-traffic region) by 2026-03-18, full rollout over 7 days after smoke tests. Metric: monitor 'terminal_event_dropped:reason=seq_out_of_window' to target < 1/week per 100k streams.
Follow-up: engineering to produce a small compatibility note for SDKs describing client-side guidance (fresh session if >10 reconnects in 30s).
